Its primary strength is achieving well-balanced regularization across all space, preventing the unbalanced gradient magnitudes that degrade UDF reconstruction quality [S1].

The claim states that the primary strength is achieving well-balanced regularization across all space to prevent unbalanced gradient magnitudes that degrade UDF reconstruction quality. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'if both the rendering and sampling functions employ the same weights, the regularization (the Eikonal loss) on UDF gradients would lead to highly unbalanced gradient magnitudes on the two sides of the surface. This could significantly hamper the quality of the reconstructed UDF field. Therefore, we propose a specially-tailored sampling weight function... to achieve well-balanced regularization all over the space.' This directly supports every part of the claim.

Unlike standard rendering weights that concentrate points near the surface, this function distributes more sampling weights before the intersection points to prevent unbalanced gradient magnitudes on the two sides of the surface, which would otherwise hamper UDF quality [S1].

The claim states that unlike standard rendering weights which concentrate points near the surface, the proposed sampling weight function distributes more weights before intersection points to prevent unbalanced gradient magnitudes. This could significantly hamper the quality of the reconstructed UDF field. Therefore, we propose a specially-tailored sampling weight function... to achieve well-balanced regularization all over the space.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
